extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers and students interested in film censorship and film history
extracted.subtask_description: A country-by-country list of films that have been banned and the stated reasons for their bans; documents the grounds censorship boards, courts, or governments cited (e.g., violence, politics, religion, sexual content). Useful for understanding common legal/social rationales for film prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic and excessive violence
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because of graphic violence or 'excessive graphic violence'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (banned because of graphic violence), Child's Play (banned due to excessive graphic violence), Cannibal Holocaust (banned for extremely violent content and on-screen killings of animals). Typical guidance: works with extreme gore or realistic depictions of mutilation are frequently refused classification or removed until cuts are made; distributors sometimes release edited cuts to obtain restricted adult classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual content and nudity / pornographic content
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for sexual content, nudity, or being classified as pornographic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Salò, or the 120 Days of Sodom (banned for graphic violence and nudity), In the Realm of the Senses (banned for graphic sex scenes), some films explicitly banned for advocating pornography. Often results in X/18 classification or outright prohibition; may be subject to re-editing to achieve certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual content involving minors or adolescents
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because of depiction of sexual activity involving adolescents or minors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Mais ne nous délivrez pas du mal (banned for depiction of violence and sexuality involving adolescents). Authorities cite protection of young people and public morality; such content frequently leads to refusal of classification or criminal concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual violence / depictions of rape or sexual assault
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for showing sexual violence or scenes that depict rape/sexual assault.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cat Sick Blues (banned because of a scene in which a woman is orally raped to death), I Spit on Your Grave (banned for tending to promote/support use of violence to compel sexual conduct). Guidance: scenes combining sexual violence with gratification or entertainment value are explicitly flagged as promoting harm and may be removed or banned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necrophilia / sexual conduct with dead persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the publication 'promotes and supports sexual conduct with or upon the body of a dead person.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Nekromantik 2 (banned for promoting necrophilia). Authorities treat necrophilia as especially objectionable sexual content leading to refusal of classification or prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bestiality / sexual conduct with animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because it 'promotes and supports bestiality' or contains sexual acts with animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Vase de Noces (banned because the film 'promotes and supports bestiality'). Such depictions are treated as criminal/objectionable content and often lead to permanent bans.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen animal cruelty and real animal killings
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for very high-impact violence including actual on-screen killings of animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Cannibal Holocaust (banned for extremely violent content and actual on-screen killings of animals). Film boards often treat real-animal-harm footage as a distinct ground for prohibition and refusal of classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion/support of sexual exploitation of children or young persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the work 'tends to promote and support the exploitation of children and young persons for sexual purposes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Puni Puni Poemy (banned on grounds of promoting exploitation of children and young persons for sexual purposes). Such grounds can lead to criminal prohibition of possession/distribution as well as refusal of classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obscenity / indecency
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the content is obscene or 'contrary to public decency' or 'indecent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Tarzoon: Shame of the Jungle (banned for content contrary to public decency), various films labeled 'obscene' (e.g., Last Tango in Paris). Obscenity standards vary by jurisdiction but often lead to classification refusal until edits are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blasphemy and offensive religious content
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for blasphemous content or depiction of prophets that is offensive to religious belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Ten Commandments (banned in Maldives for depiction of Moses), The Last Temptation of Christ (banned in several countries for offending Christians), Innocence of Muslims (banned for being blasphemous and critical of Islam). Religious offence can trigger bans, sometimes following pressure from clerics or religious groups, and may be contested legally.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGBTQ content (homosexuality / same-sex depictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because of depictions of homosexuality, same-sex kisses, or LGBTQ themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Rafiki (initially banned in Kenya for depictions of homosexuality), Lightyear (banned in multiple countries for a brief lesbian kiss), multiple titles banned for 'promoting homosexuality'. Many jurisdictions explicitly exclude or restrict LGBTQ representation, leading to bans or reclassification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transgender or non-binary representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned due to inclusion of transgender/non-binary characters, symbols, or positive representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse (frames featuring a transgender flag with 'Protect Trans Kids' briefly shown led to bans in some places), Talk to Me banned in some jurisdictions for inclusion of a non-binary/transmasculine actor. Such instances show bans can target even brief or symbolic representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political content / criticism of government / anti-regime material
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film criticizes the government, colonial rule, or could inspire revolutionary/anti-government sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Afrique 50 (banned for criticizing French colonial rule), The Battle of Algiers (banned for pro-Algerian/anticolonial message), films banned for criticizing Sukarno or other regimes. Political censorship commonly targets films judged threatening to domestic stability or diplomatic ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm to international/diplomatic relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because it was 'potentially harmful to international relations' or could harm diplomatic relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Born American (banned for being 'potentially harmful to international relations' at first), The Girl in the Kremlin (banned in Israel for potentially harming relations with Moscow). Governments sometimes cite foreign-policy concerns to justify bans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insulting or defamatory content toward individuals or groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for libelous or personally insulting material (including offensive dubs or jokes about named individuals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Shrek 2 (briefly banned because a Hebrew dub joke insulted singer David D'Or, prompting legal action). Defamation or targeted insult can lead to withdrawal or censorship even where the film itself would otherwise be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative portrayal of national history / armed forces / honor
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because it damages the honor of the army, portrays national history negatively, or is considered damaging to national prestige.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Lion of the Desert (banned as damaging to the honor of the Italian Army), Rojo Amanecer (banned due to its portrayal of the 1968 student massacre). Such bans are often justified on grounds of national dignity or morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Racial/ethnic stereotyping and antisemitic content
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for being anti-Jewish, racist, or for negative stereotyping of ethnic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Jud Süss (banned for anti-Jewish/pro-Nazi content), District 9 (banned in Nigeria for alleged xenophobia/racism). Content that promotes hatred or harmful stereotyping is a common grounds for prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public order / risk of incitement
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because it threatens public order or could incite unrest (e.g., inspire revolution, disturbing civil peace).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Battleship Potemkin (banned due to fears it could inspire revolution), films banned for 'stimulating sectarian and partisan zealotries and disturbing civil peace' (Lebanon). Authorities may block films they believe could catalyze protests or violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental health / public safety concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for reasons tied to mental health or because it was judged harmful to mental wellbeing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Dirty Harry (banned in Finland in 1972 for violence and mental health reasons). Boards sometimes cite potential psychological harm as justification for prohibition or restrictive classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depictions of real human death or genuine human death footage
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the film 'entirely banned for the possible inclusion of scenes of genuine human death' or contains real human death footage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Ultime grida dalla savana (banned for possible inclusion of scenes of genuine human death). Real death footage is often treated as uniquely objectionable and may trigger bans regardless of other content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion/support of torture or sadistic violence combined with sexual gratification
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because scenes 'fuse an act of extreme violence with sexual gratification' or tend to promote/support torture and sadistic violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Hostel: Part II (banned due to a scene fusing extreme violence with sexual gratification; later allowed after excision). Boards treat such fusions as likely to promote harm and may require removal of specific scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural, classification, or registration grounds (refused classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Refused classification or banned because the film was not registered, refused classification, or for procedural issues unrelated to content per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Sausage Party (refused classification for indecency according to some reports), films never registered with a censor board may be considered illegal to distribute. Administrative/registration noncompliance can be grounds for prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or technical legal objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned for copyright technicalities or legal objections from rights-holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Carmen Jones (banned due to a technicality in copyright laws on order of the estate of Georges Bizet). Legal ownership disputes or copyright restrictions can lead to temporary or sustained removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic/political imagery (colors/symbols construed as rebel support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because symbolic elements (colors, imagery) are construed as support for rebel groups or politically sensitive movements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: The Simpsons Movie (banned in Myanmar over the 'juxtaposition of the colors yellow and red', seen as support for rebel groups). Even nonverbal symbols can trigger censorship when politically loaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Casting-related bans (inclusion of particular actors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because of the inclusion of specific actors (e.g., actors associated with a disliked state) or casting choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Wonder Woman and Justice League (banned in some countries because they cast Israeli actress Gal Gadot), Ben-Hur (banned in some Arab League states because an actress was Israeli). Casting can become a reason for boycott or bans tied to geopolitical tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychosocial harm / erosion of empathy concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Banned because the work is seen as likely to cause erosion of empathy or normalize cruel behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Maniac (banned in New Zealand because the OFLC felt the film's first-person portrayal tacitly invited enjoyment of cruel behaviour and could erode empathy). Some censorship rationales focus on downstream social/psychological effects rather than discrete content categories.
